about.title: Mill Valley Slip & Fall Claims
about.longDescription: Mill Valley's mix of hillside walkways, downtown shops along E Blithedale Avenue, and older properties tucked near Camino Alto creates plenty of opportunities for uneven pavement, loose stair treads, or spilled liquids to go unaddressed. When that happens and someone gets hurt, California law asks whether the property owner knew, or reasonably should have known, about the hazard and failed to fix it or warn visitors. Proving that notice is often the hardest part of a premises liability case, which is why photos of the hazard, witness names, and store surveillance footage matter so much in the days right after a fall. LawProactive doesn't practice law itself; we're a free connection service that matches injured Mill Valley residents with an independent attorney who can evaluate what happened, request that footage before it's erased, and explain your options. There's no cost to find out where you stand, and no obligation to move forward.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney About Notice and Evidence

items.title: Notice Is the Hard Part to Prove
items.desc: California requires showing the property owner knew or should have known about the hazard. An attorney knows how to dig up maintenance logs, prior complaints, or inspection records that establish that.

items.title: Video Disappears Fast
items.desc: Many businesses overwrite surveillance footage within days or weeks. Getting a preservation letter out quickly can be the difference between having proof and having nothing.

items.title: Comparative Fault Affects Your Recovery
items.desc: California allows recovery even if you were partly at fault, but your share of blame can reduce what you're owed. An attorney can push back on unfair fault arguments from the property owner's insurer.

items.question: How long do I have to file a slip and fall claim in Mill Valley?
items.answer: Generally you have two years from the date of the fall under California law. That window shrinks significantly if the property involved is owned by a public entity, like a city sidewalk or public building, so it's worth checking sooner rather than later.

items.question: What if I fell at a shop on Miller Avenue or E Blithedale and didn't get anyone's name?
items.answer: It happens, but it's not fatal to a claim. An attorney can often pull surveillance footage, employee schedules, and other records to reconstruct what happened, though acting quickly improves the odds that evidence still exists.

items.question: Does it matter if I was partly responsible for the fall?
items.answer: Not entirely. California uses pure comparative fault, meaning you can still recover even if you share some blame, though your compensation may be reduced by your percentage of fault. An attorney can help make sure that percentage isn't inflated unfairly.

items.question: Is there a cost to talk to LawProactive about my fall?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is a free service that connects you with an independent attorney, and attorneys in the network work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless you recover something.
